q: A roof lies between two opposite walls of the same height. How much wall area is added to the roof area for drain sizing?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Rain driven against one wall is balanced by shelter from the other, so no wall area is added. Walls beside a roof catch driving rain and shed it onto the roof, so part of their area is added when sizing the drains.

q: What minimum total inlet area must a dome-type roof strainer have?
o: 2 times the area of the outlet pipe
1.5 times the area of the outlet pipe
Equal to the area of the outlet pipe
3 times the area of the outlet pipe
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Leaves collect on the dome, so its openings must exceed the pipe area. Flat roof-deck strainers need 2 times.

q: Which way does a leader (conductor) carry rainwater?
o: From the downspout to the gutter
From the storm sewer to the building
From the gutter to the downspout
From the roof drain to the vent stack
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Leaders and conductors carry roof water from the gutter or roof drain down toward the storm drain.

q: How high above the roof surface must a roof drain dome strainer rise?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: The raised dome keeps taking water even when leaves and debris pile up around its base.

q: May rainwater piping be used as a vent, soil or waste pipe?
o: Yes, if it is cast iron
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Mixing systems sends sewer gas and sewage into storm lines, or storm water into the sanitary system.

q: What rainfall intensity does the plumbing code use for the Manila area when sizing rainwater piping?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Pipe sizes in the code tables are read from roof area and rainfall intensity.

q: What is storm water?
o: Waste water from sinks and showers
Water drained from a swimming pool
The part of rainfall that runs off over the surface
Water from a building's cooling tower
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Storm water is collected by roof drains, gutters and area drains and kept out of the sanitary system.

q: What must roof drains be made of?
o: Cast iron, copper or other corrosion-resistant material
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Roof drains sit in standing water and debris, so they must not corrode.

q: What is rainwater piping sized from?
o: Rainfall intensity and the roof area drained
The height of the building only
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: The code tables give the roof area each pipe size can drain at a given rainfall intensity.

q: From what point does "rainwater piping" (as against the building's leaders) begin under the code?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: As with the sanitary side, the storm line changes name 0.60 m outside the building.

q: What is a downspout?
o: The horizontal gutter along the eave
The strainer over a roof drain
The vertical part of a rainwater conductor
The pipe from the building to the public storm sewer
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: A downspout carries water from the gutter down the face of the building.

q: A roof is enclosed by walls on three sides. What is added to the roof area for drain sizing?
o: Nothing, as walls on three sides shelter the roof
100% of the area of all three walls
50% of the inner wall area below the top of the lowest wall, plus the wall area above it
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Walls beside a roof catch driving rain and shed it onto the roof, so part of their area is added when sizing the drains.

q: What is the house storm sewer?
o: The pipe from the building's storm drainage to the public storm sewer
The vertical pipe from the gutter to the ground
The pipe from the building to the public sanitary sewer
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: It is the storm-side twin of the building sewer.

q: Why do downspouts in high-rise buildings need stronger pipe?
o: A full column of water builds up high hydrostatic pressure at the bottom
Rainwater is more acidic at height
Codes require the same pipe as fire standpipes
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: If a downspout backs up, water pressure at the base rises about 10 kPa for every metre of height.

q: A roof has one wall rising beside it. What is added to the roof area for drain sizing?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Walls beside a roof catch driving rain and shed it onto the roof, so part of their area is added when sizing the drains.

q: For the side of a tall building exposed to rain, what area is used for drain sizing?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Wind-driven rain strikes a tall face at an angle, so half of the face is counted.

q: What is the lightest galvanized sheet metal allowed for downspouts on low buildings?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Higher gauge numbers are thinner. Gauge 26 is the thinnest allowed, and only on low buildings.

q: A roof is enclosed by walls on all four sides. What wall area is added for drain sizing?
o: None below the top of the lowest wall; only the wall area above it
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Walls beside a roof catch driving rain and shed it onto the roof, so part of their area is added when sizing the drains.

q: A 200 m² roof has two adjacent walls rising beside it, with a total area of 80 m². What area is used to size the drains?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Walls beside a roof catch driving rain and shed it onto the roof, so part of their area is added when sizing the drains.
steps: Two adjacent walls: add 35% of their total area

q: Which materials may be used for rainwater piping in medium-height buildings?
o: Galvanized iron, cast iron, DWV copper, ABS or PVC-DWV
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Medium-height buildings need pipe that holds some pressure, so light sheet metal is not enough.

q: What minimum total inlet area must a flat roof-deck strainer have?
o: 2 times the area of the outlet pipe
1.5 times the area of the outlet pipe
Equal to the area of the outlet pipe
4 times the area of the outlet pipe
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Flat strainers on sun decks clog faster than domes, so they need more open area.

q: Which of these is NOT listed as a downspout material?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Downspouts may be cast iron, galvanized steel, iron, brass, copper, lead, ABS or PVC-DWV. Clay is for buried sewers.

q: Which parts of a storm drainage system must be tested?
o: Roof drains, overflow drains and rainwater piping
Nothing, since storm water is not sewage
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Leaks inside a building damage it just as sewage leaks do, so storm piping is tested too.

q: Which areas must be provided with storm drainage?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Any paved or roofed area that collects rain must drain to an approved disposal point.

q: What must an interior roof drain be?
o: Any material, since it is inside
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: A leak inside the building would soak ceilings and walls, so interior drains are cast iron and watertight.

q: What is the purpose of a storm drainage system?
o: To carry sewage to the septic tank
To collect storm water and discharge it to an approved disposal point
To vent the sanitary drainage system
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Storm water may go to a storm sewer, a drainage ditch or a harvesting tank, but never into the sanitary system.

q: A roof lies between two opposite walls of different heights. What is added to the roof area for drain sizing?
o: 50% of the higher wall's area above the top of the lower wall
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Only the part of the taller wall that is not sheltered by the lower wall catches extra rain.

q: A roof has two adjacent walls rising beside it. What is added to the roof area for drain sizing?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 11
n: Walls beside a roof catch driving rain and shed it onto the roof, so part of their area is added when sizing the drains.
